About AAWFIP

The Aquatic Animal Welfare Funding Intelligence Platform is a research tool that profiles funders relevant to aquatic animal welfare — trusts, foundations, and grantmaking bodies — and scores them by priority, fit, and funding activity. Use it to identify likely funders, upload a new project brief (PDF/Word) to get it matched against every funder, track application deadlines and status, and keep notes as you research and apply. A separate Competitiveness engine assesses how strong your own application is likely to be — a readiness score, a gap analysis against a strong applicant, a simulated reviewer critique, and a prioritised improvement roadmap — before you invest months preparing a proposal.

Build status — 26 organisations researched and integrated. The Module 2 profile schema is fully wired: Wellcome Trust, Tiny Beam Fund, Animal Charity Evaluators (ACE), Templeton World Charity Foundation (TWCF), EA Funds — Animal Welfare Fund (AWF), Coefficient Giving, the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation, the Walton Family Foundation, the Animal Welfare Foundation (British Veterinary Association), the Animal Welfare Institute (AWI), the AZA Animal Care & Wellbeing Grants Fund, the Gates Foundation, USAID, EU Horizon Europe, Senterra Funders (formerly Farmed Animal Funders), the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), The Joanna Toole Foundation (JTF), The Pew Charitable Trusts, The Rockefeller Foundation, Morris Animal Foundation, Norad (the Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation), Compassion in World Farming (CIWF), The Marchig Animal Welfare Trust, The David and Lucile Packard Foundation, Science for Animal Welfare (formerly the Universities Federation for Animal Welfare, UFAW), and its sister charity the Humane Slaughter Association (HSA) each have a complete profile — click-through from cards, full profile view, working search and filters, localStorage-backed personal notes, and PDF export via the browser's print dialog (Export PDF on a profile, or Export summary report on the dashboard). Every number in the stat strip and aside reflects live data from AAWFIP_DATA — nothing here is hand-typed. Per-profile strategic fit, success-likelihood scoring, and marketing-positioning sections (Modules 3 and 5) are implemented within each profile, and the standalone project-matching dashboard view (Module 4) is now live. The Funding Calendar (Module 7) parses each funder's own deadline and scheme-status text for explicit dates and lays them out chronologically, with a separate watch-list for rolling/invitation-only funders that carry no fixed date. Notes & Tracker (Module 8) is now live: a consolidated, exportable view of every note saved across profiles, plus an opportunity tracker and change-detection layer that snapshots each funder's status, deadline, priority, score, funding schemes, and stated remit on first visit and diffs the live data against that snapshot on every later visit \u2014 it cannot poll the live web, but it will surface anything that changes in this file itself. LinkedIn/programme-contact intelligence (Module 6) is intentionally limited to what funders publish themselves, per the platform's no-invented-data standard. All eight planned modules are now built. The Applicant Competitiveness Intelligence Engine is also now live, under the Competitiveness tab: a twelve-part self-assessment — an initial readiness intake, then a readiness score, a Top 10% competitiveness predictor, a competitive gap analysis, a simulated reviewer critique, competitor benchmarking, a proposal weakness detector, an impact strength index, a collaboration strength index, a funding-probability scenario planner, and a personalised improvement roadmap, plus a Top 5% checklist — with an executive dashboard that pulls every module's output onto one screen. It runs entirely from your own intake answers and is independent of the funder database above; nothing in it is drawn from AAWFIP_DATA or any external source. Collaboration & Networking Intelligence (Module 9) is also now live, under its own tab: every organisation in AAWFIP_DATA is scored on collaboration/networking potential (0–100, via collabIntel) independently of whether it is a funder — non-funder organisations are researched and scored here too, filterable separately from funders, with the same score shown on each organisation's own profile.

Upload & Match

Upload a project brief (PDF or Word) and AAWFIP will scan it and rank every funder in the database across twelve independent matching dimensions — research theme, strategic priority, geographic fit, organisational mission fit, beneficiary fit, objectives alignment, expected impact alignment, methodology alignment, applicant eligibility fit, budget suitability, project duration fit, and collaboration & partnership fit — then combine them into a weighted overall score. Files are read entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded to a server.

My Projects

Keep a real record of your own projects here. This is the source of truth the Strategic Intelligence sync reads from. Every project — whether typed in below, pasted as a full brief, or uploaded via Upload & Match — is stored in the same standard format: Organisation, Type, Summary, Objectives, Study design & methods, Countries, Species, Keywords, Funding stage, Budget, Deliverables (see the Peri-harvest Welfare record for a worked example).

Collaboration & Networking Intelligence

Every organisation in the database evaluated on collaboration and networking potential, independently of whether it offers a grant. Funders are still scored as funders elsewhere on this platform, but the score below reflects something different: how genuinely useful this organisation, or the named people inside it, could be as a collaborator, introduction, or professional connection \u2014 named contacts, sourced overlap with your own work, warm-introduction threads, and openness to being approached. Non-funders (research bodies, networks, associations with no grant programme) are evaluated here too, since a poor funding fit is not the same as a poor networking fit.

Method: this score is an AI-generated, evidence-informed estimate \u2014 not a statistic, not a relationship-strength guarantee, and not drawn from any data source beyond what is already cited in each organisation's own profile (named contacts, published team pages, grant-history overlaps). It never invents a contact, credential, or connection that isn't already sourced elsewhere in that profile. Score bands: 80\u2013100 Very high, 60\u201379 High, 40\u201359 Moderate, 20\u201339 Low, 0\u201319 Minimal.

Funding Calendar

Every date below is pulled directly from each funder's own deadline and scheme-status text already in AAWFIP_DATA — nothing is estimated or invented. Funders with no extractable date sit in the Rolling / unscheduled section. Click any category below to expand or collapse it.

Open (deadline within 30 days) Upcoming (more than 30 days away) Recently closed (within 90 days) Past funding (more than 90 days closed) Rolling / unscheduled
Method: every entry is extracted by scanning each funder's own deadline field and each funding-scheme's own status text for an explicit calendar date. Each dated entry is then sorted into a category by how many days its date sits from today: Open (0–30 days from now), Upcoming (more than 30 days from now), Recently closed (0–90 days ago), or Past funding (more than 90 days ago). The original wording is shown in full underneath each date so no nuance (rolling-after, by-invitation, etc.) is lost in the extraction. A funder with several schemes can appear more than once — each row is one dated scheme, not one funder.

Notes & Tracker

What this can and can't honestly do: this file itself has no live connection to the web — it's a static HTML file, and always will be. The "Opportunity tracker" and "Change detection" sections below compare the funder data currently loaded in this file against the last snapshot you reviewed, and flag anything that's new or changed each time you (or Claude) update this file with fresh research. The "Live web check" section further down is different: it's optional, and when set up (see that section), it reads a snapshot produced by a scheduled check that actually visits each funder's real website — see that section for what it can and can't do on its own.

Method: on first visit this device captures a baseline snapshot of every funder's status, deadline, priority tier, overall score, funding-scheme details, and stated remit/priority areas. Every later visit re-reads the live AAWFIP_DATA in this file and diffs it against that saved baseline \u2014 nothing is simulated or guessed. Click "Mark all as reviewed" to reset the baseline to the current data. Notes are the same ones saved from each organisation's profile, saved locally in this browser only.

Applicant Competitiveness Intelligence Engine

This module doesn't write grant applications. It assesses how competitive an applicant is likely to be before they invest months preparing a proposal — surfacing strengths, weaknesses, missing competitive elements, and the highest-value next actions, the way an experienced grant reviewer would.

Funding Readiness Assessment

Start your competitiveness assessment

A short, multi-section intake — applicant profile, track record, team, project, impact, and partnerships — feeds every score, gap analysis, and recommendation in this engine. Nothing here is fabricated: every estimate is framed as evidence-informed, based on recognised grant-review principles and what you enter below.

                        How to use AAWFIP

                        1. Browse the Dashboard — scan high-priority and recently updated funders, or scroll the full database. Use the search bar or sidebar filters (priority, status, region, theme) to narrow the list, and the quick-filter chips for common views like "Open now" or "Favourites".
                        2. Open a profile — click any organisation card for its full profile: funding schemes, eligibility, strategic fit, and success-likelihood scoring. Add personal notes there, and use Export PDF to save a copy.
                        3. Upload a new project — on Upload & Match, drop in a project brief as a PDF or Word document. AAWFIP reads it in your browser and ranks every funder by how closely their published remit overlaps with it — a fast first pass for projects that aren't in the platform yet. If the document uses the standard project headings (Organisation, Type, Summary, Objectives, Study design & methods, Countries, Species, Keywords, Funding stage, Budget, Deliverables), those sections are also filed automatically into the matching fields on the project's My Projects record — the same fields you'd fill in by pasting a brief there directly.
                        4. Match your researched projects — switch to Project Matching to compare your existing project portfolio against each funder's remit and see which opportunities fit best.
                        5. Check deadlines — the Funding Calendar lays out upcoming deadlines chronologically, with a separate watch-list for rolling or invitation-only funders.
                        6. Track changes — Notes & Tracker collects every note you've saved in one place, and flags what's new or changed in the funder data since your last visit.
                        7. Adjust scoring weights — click the gear icon in the header to see and change how much each of the 10 scorecard criteria counts toward a funder's overall opportunity score.
                        8. Export a summary — use "Export summary report" on the dashboard to print or save a PDF overview of the full database.

                        Applicant Competitiveness Intelligence Engine

                        1. Start the assessment — open Competitiveness and answer the readiness intake once; your answers drive every module below.
                        2. Read your results — a readiness score, gap analysis, simulated reviewer critique, and competitor benchmarking show where you're strong and where you're not.
                        3. Follow the roadmap — the personalised improvement roadmap and Top 5% checklist turn those results into a prioritised to-do list.
                        4. Check the dashboard — the executive dashboard pulls every module's output onto one screen, and can be printed or exported like a profile.
